questions.q: Which set correctly names the five drivers of trends in society, remembered as SPEEG?
questions.explanation: Trends are driven by Social, Political, Economic, Environmental and Global forces — SPEEG. Historical and cultural influences are also significant but get their own episode as the era factor, so today's focus is these five contemporary drivers.

questions.q: What are the primary considerations when designing products to meet the needs of society?
questions.explanation: Designing for the needs of society means responding to broad social trends and expectations that affect the whole community. Individual, cultural and environmental factors are relevant, but social trends are the primary consideration when designing for society as a whole.

questions.q:
A coffee table has been designed with a touch screen computer built into it.

Which factor is most likely to have influenced this design?
questions.explanation: Building interactive touch-screen technology into furniture responds to social trends in how people use and integrate technology in everyday living. Aesthetic, safety and environmental factors are not the main driver of adding a computer to a coffee table.

questions.q: As a product approaches the end of its life cycle, what factor contributes most to its decline in acceptance?
questions.explanation: As tastes, needs and fashions change, shifting social trends make a product less desirable and drive its decline at the end of its life cycle. Poor design, materials and manufacturing relate to how a product is made rather than why consumers stop accepting it over time.

questions.q: The trend towards sustainable design is most directly driven by which SPEEG force?
options: The political driver — government incentives for renewables
The environmental driver — concern for sustainability, climate and resources
The global driver — globalised supply chains
The economic driver — cost pressures in a downturn
questions.explanation: Sustainable design is pushed mainly by the environmental driver — concern for sustainability, climate and resources — supported by social conscience. It steers designers toward recyclable materials, energy efficiency and life-cycle thinking, while raising the issue of cost.

questions.q: In an H2.1 answer, what is the difference between naming a trend and discussing it?
options: Naming lists the trend's benefits; discussing lists its drawbacks
Naming just states the trend exists; discussing analyses the issues it raises — the opportunities and the problems
Naming uses a case study; discussing uses statistics
There is no difference; the syllabus treats them as the same skill
questions.explanation: The syllabus verb is 'discuss the issues arising', so naming a trend (stating it exists) caps low. A strong answer names the trend, classifies its SPEEG driver, then discusses the issues — both the opportunities and the problems — for designers, workers and society.

questions.q: From memory: what are the five drivers of trends in society (SPEEG)?
keyPoints: Social — changes in society, demographics, multiculturalism, social conscience, values.
Political — government policy, regulation, the political climate.
Economic — economic conditions, wealth, socio-economic status, cost pressures.
Environmental — concern for sustainability, climate and resources.
Global — globalisation, international markets, global supply chains, world events.
questions.explanation: If you recalled all five letters of SPEEG and what each stands for, grade yourself Good or Easy. SPEEG keeps you from missing a driver, and you can add that historical-cultural influences (the era factor) also matter.

questions.q: From memory: why is it important for designers to monitor trends in society?
keyPoints: Trends shape what consumers need and want.
A designer who keeps up with trends creates products that are relevant, timely and commercially successful.
A designer who ignores trends risks producing something outdated or mistimed — like an innovation launched as the market moves the other way (e.g. the Microsoft Zune against the shift to downloads).
questions.explanation: The key point is that designers monitor trends to stay relevant. If you linked monitoring to timely, commercially successful design and noted the risk of mistiming, grade Good or Easy.

questions.q: Explain how an environmental trend has influenced design and production. (3 marks)
questions.modelAnswer: The environmental trend, driven by growing concern for sustainability and climate, has influenced design and production by pushing designers toward recyclable and renewable materials, energy-efficient products, and life-cycle thinking that minimises waste and carbon footprint. For example, many products are now designed for recyclability and repair rather than disposal. However, this trend raises the issue of cost, since sustainable materials and processes are often more expensive, creating tension between environmental and financial considerations.

criteria.descriptor: Identifies the environmental driver behind the trend (concern for sustainability/climate).
Explains how the trend shifts design/production, with an example (recyclable materials, energy efficiency, life-cycle thinking).
Discusses an issue the trend raises (e.g. cost — the environmental-versus-financial tension).

questions.explanation: Markers want the influence plus an issue, not just 'people care about the environment'. Identify the driver, explain how it shifts design with an example, and discuss the issue it raises.

questions.q: Discuss ONE social trend that can affect the design of a new product.
questions.modelAnswer: One social trend is the use of artificial intelligence. AI can generate images and concepts from written descriptions, which is a good way to stimulate design ideas — but the concept is not the designer's own work, raising authorship and intellectual-property issues. (Other trends worth discussing: eco/green materials, fast fashion and its waste, and the throw-away society of constant technology upgrades.)

criteria.descriptor: Discusses the effect of a social trend on the design of a new product
Demonstrates an understanding of a social trend that can affect the design of a new product
Demonstrates an understanding of a social trend

questions.explanation: This is the syllabus skill for H2.1: don't just name a social trend, discuss the issues it raises for designing a new product. Name the trend, then analyse the opportunities and problems it creates.
